parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
An electrochemical cell is set up to measure $E^\ominus_{\text{cell}}$ of a cell consisting of an $\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}$ half-cell and a $\text{Cl}_2/\text{Cl}^-$ half-cell.

Draw a labelled diagram of this electrochemical cell.

Include all necessary substances. It is **not** necessary to state conditions used.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The cell reaction for the electrochemical cell in (b) is shown.

$$\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow 2\text{Fe}^{3+} + 2\text{Cl}^- \qquad E^\ominus_{\text{cell}} = +0.59\text{ V}$$

Calculate $\Delta G^\ominus$, in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, for this cell reaction.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem:
Another experiment is set up using the same electrochemical cell.

In this experiment the $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ concentration is $0.15\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$. All other concentrations remain at their standard values.

The Nernst equation is shown.

$$E = E^\ominus + (0.059/z) \log \frac{[\text{oxidised species}]}{[\text{reduced species}]}$$

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
Use the Nernst equation to calculate the electrode potential, $E$, for the $\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}$ half-cell in this experiment.

[$E^\ominus$: $\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+} = +0.77\text{ V}$]

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Use your answer to (d)(i) to calculate $E_{\text{cell}}$ for this electrochemical cell.
